title: Incident Triage Canvas: Adaptive Error Taxonomy & Payload Sampler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Design an 'Incident Triage Canvas' in the Redwood Console that helps engineers rapidly understand failure modes, see representative payloads, and run lightweight retry/playback experiments without leaving the console. The Canvas bundles three coordinated surfaces: (1) an Adaptive Error Taxonomy that groups failures into human-readable clusters with signal-backed reasons (e.g., model OOM, rate-limit fallback, unexpected schema, LLM hallucination), (2) a Payload Sampler that surfaces representative request/response snapshots and a lightweight diff view (snapshot vs canonical expectation), and (3) a Representative Failure Carousel for quick A/B retry attempts across model variants or rollout buckets. This ticket covers low-fidelity to mid-fidelity prototypes, a design review, and handoff artifacts for engineering.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Maya: Kickoff meeting notes: aligned with PM on scope; primary success metric is mean triage time reduction by 30% for P1 incidents. Need to coordinate with ENG for telemetry surface (failure tags + canonical expectation signals).

2025-01-18 - Arjun: Uploaded mid-fi prototype to Figma. Core interactions: hover-to-decompose taxonomy cluster, open-sampler to view 3 representative payloads selected by recency + anomaly score, quick-retry button with model variant selector. Asked design to add a privacy scrubber toggle for sampled payloads.

2025-01-22 - PM (Jordan Blake): Requested additional UX for rollout-aware failures (show bucket, percentage impacted) and integration with Rollouts dashboard. Added dependency PM-4123 for rollout metadata contract.

2025-01-24 - Eng (Lina Gomez): Raised performance constraint: sampling must not add >50ms to request list queries; suggested server-side precomputed representative snapshots (ENG-1987). Also called out redaction rules for PII — we should surface scrubbing presets.

2025-01-28 - Design review: Feedback from Alex (SRE) and Priya (Applied ML): prefer combined timeline + taxonomy view; taxonomy should be editable filters (merge/split clusters) for power users. Action: deliver two variants in next prototype: (A) taxonomy-first (cluster list) and (B) timeline-first (ordered incidents with on-hover cluster breadcrumbs).

2025-01-30 - Maya: Implemented variant A and B in Figma; added microcopy for privacy scrubber and sampling rationale. Added acceptance criteria and sample user flows. Pushed updated link in attachments.

2025-02-02 - Arjun: Conducted 3 informal hallway tests with support engineers. Outcomes: sampler is valuable; users asked for 'open in inspector' link that opens the full payload in Debug Workbench. Also requested direct link to create a replay ticket. Added follow-up tasks for engineering and PM.

2025-02-02 - Decision: Proceed with taxonomy-first default for console-2025.02 but keep timeline-first as an opt-in expert mode. Engineering to implement server-side sampling pipeline and scrubbers before UI launch.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive Error Taxonomy renders clusters with human-friendly labels and top-3 signals (count, error-rate delta, representative model variant).
Payload Sampler surfaces up to 5 representative snapshots per cluster with inline scrubber controls and a link to full Debug Workbench payload view.
Representative Failure Carousel supports single-click retry across model variants and attaches persisted notes to the retry request for auditability.
Design handoff includes high/medium/low-fidelity prototypes, copy, edge-case flows (no-sample, scrubbed-only, high-volume clusters), and a dev checklist for telemetry and privacy constraints.
Design signoff from PM, Eng lead, and SRE obtained and attached to the ticket.
